Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, we put together a concise commercial approach to move Atlas from your current monthly consumption model to a 12–24 month annual prepay while addressing the key risks you raised (budget timing, ramp variability, and overage protection).

High-level proposal (attached: Redwood_Annual_Term_Summary_v1.xlsx):
- Term: 12 months initial with option to extend to 24 months at reprice.
- Pricing: blended term discount on list pricing tied to committed spend bands.
- Ramp smoothing: monthly usage true-up with a capped overage buffer; step-up credits if you exceed forecast early.
- Risk-share: limited consumption protection for first 90 days and a 60-day exit window for material deltas (subject to conditions).
- Payment: annual prepay preferred; we can offer quarterly invoicing with net-30 for ARR accounting reasons (see Marcus for finance constraints).

Next steps: please review and confirm which of the three commitment bands (Conservative / Target / Accelerated) you want us to model. Ben and I can prepare a concession matrix and a redline-ready term sheet.

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the quick notes. Wanted to propose a concrete concession set to make a prepay work while protecting you on utilization: (attached: Concession_Matrix_v3.pdf)

Offer (summary):
- Commitment bands: $120k/year (Conservative), $240k/year (Target), $480k/year (Accelerated).
- Discounting: 8% off list at Conservative; 12% at Target; 18% at Accelerated for year 1. Year 2 reprice with a floor discount of 6% (if you elect 24-month term, we can lock 2nd-year pricing).
- Usage smoothing: monthly true-up with a 12% monthly overage cap (Atlas pays actual usage above committed monthly forecast, but not more than 12% in any month). Any overage above the annual committed total will be invoiced quarterly at list.
- Under-utilization credit: if actual annual consumption is <70% of committed, we credit 30% of the delta back as a service credit to be applied to next quarter usage (applies only to the first contract year).
- Pilot clause: 60-day proof-of-value with a 75% refund of any unused portion of the first quarter if baseline KPIs are not met.

We can also structure quarterly invoicing on the annual amount (prepay amortized over four invoices) if that helps your procurement cadence, with an earlier signature window to lock the pricing.

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for flagging the procurement window. To bridge fiscal timing concerns while keeping the economics of a prepay, here's a compromise we often use:

- Execution: sign a 12-month agreement now to lock pricing. Payment can be one of two options: (A) annual prepay (single invoice), or (B) quarterly invoices on the prepay amount (amortized) with net-30 terms. Either option requires signed agreement to lock discount.
- Ramp schedule: we will build a three-month onboarding baseline; if your first 90 days are <60% of forecast, we apply a one-time onboarding credit equal to 25% of the variance (service credit).
- Step-up: if you accelerate to the next spend band during the term, we will apply a retroactive pro-rated discount for the remainder of the year.
- PO / procurement: please share the PO in the format you prefer (we can accept a PO and follow with a DocuSign execution).

I uploaded a usage baseline template to help model (link: https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2b3cATL-usage-baseline). If you can populate the next 6 months by end of week we will run the precise amortization and credit math.
